notes.summary: Percentages covers converting between fractions and percents, percentage change, successive changes, and applications such as marks, elections, population, depreciation, expenditure and consumption. SSC CGL asks 1-3 direct questions on it, and the same ideas drive profit-loss, interest and data interpretation.
keyPoints: % change = (change ÷ original value) × 100. The base is always the original value.
If A is r% more than B, then B is r/(100 + r) × 100 % less than A (25% more gives 20% less). If A is r% less than B, then B is r/(100 − r) × 100 % more than A (20% less gives 25% more).
Successive changes of a% and b% give a net change of a + b + ab/100, with decreases taken as negative. Example: +20% then −10% gives 20 − 10 − 2 = +8%.
If the price rises by r% and expenditure must stay the same, consumption must fall by r/(100 + r) × 100 %. A 25% rise needs a 20% cut.
Population and depreciation: value after n years = P(1 ± r/100)ⁿ. Example: 10,000 growing at 10% a year becomes 12,100 in 2 years.
x% of y = y% of x. Example: 12% of 75 = 75% of 12 = 9.
Marks questions: the difference between two percentages equals the difference in marks, which gives the maximum marks.
Percentage points are not the same as percent change. A rate falling from 8% to 6% is 2 percentage points but a 25% decrease.
Two sets: passed in both = 100 − (failed in A + failed in B − failed in both).
traps: Using the new value instead of the original value as the base for % change.
Adding successive percentage changes directly instead of using a + b + ab/100.
Confusing a drop in percentage points with a percentage decrease.
In election questions with invalid votes, applying the winner's % to the total votes instead of the valid votes.
Assuming that 'A is 25% more than B' means 'B is 25% less than A'.
notes.examTip: Memorise fraction-percentage equivalents up to 1/20. Most SSC percentage questions then become a single multiplication.

questions.text: What percentage of 1.5 kg is 120 g?
questions.explanation:
Convert to the same unit first: 1.5 kg = 1,500 g.
Percentage = 120/1,500 × 100 = 8%.

questions.text: A's salary is 25% more than B's salary. By what percentage is B's salary less than A's salary?
questions.explanation:
Let B = 100. Then A = 125.
B is less than A by 25 on a base of 125.
Percentage = 25/125 × 100 = 20%.
Formula: r/(100 + r) × 100 = 25/125 × 100 = 20%.

questions.text: What is 15% of 20% of 2,000?
The population of a town is 10,000. If it increases by 10% every year, what will the population be after 2 years?
questions.explanation:
The growth is compounded, so the second year's 10% is on the new population.
After 1 year: 10,000 × 1.1 = 11,000.
After 2 years: 11,000 × 1.1 = 12,100.
Note: 12,000 is wrong because it adds 10% of the original population twice.

questions.text: 12% of 75 is equal to 75% of which number?
questions.explanation:
x% of y = y% of x, so 12% of 75 = 75% of 12.
Check: 12% of 75 = 9 and 75% of 12 = 9.
The required number is 12.

questions.text: A machine costing ₹50,000 depreciates at the rate of 10% per year. What will its value be after 2 years?
questions.explanation:
Depreciation is applied each year on the reduced value.
After 1 year: 50,000 × 0.9 = ₹45,000.
After 2 years: 45,000 × 0.9 = ₹40,500.

questions.text: A student needs 33% of the maximum marks to pass. He scored 125 marks and failed by 40 marks. What are the maximum marks?
questions.explanation:
Pass marks = 125 + 40 = 165.
33% of the maximum = 165.
Maximum marks = 165 × 100/33 = 500.

questions.text: In an examination, 30% of the students failed in Hindi, 35% failed in English and 27% failed in both subjects. What percentage of students passed in both subjects?
questions.explanation:
Failed in at least one subject = 30 + 35 − 27 = 38%.
Passed in both = 100 − 38 = 62%.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, 20% of the votes cast were declared invalid. The winner got 55% of the valid votes and won by 2,000 votes. What was the total number of votes cast?
questions.explanation:
Let the total votes be T. Valid votes = 0.8T.
The winner gets 55% and the loser 45% of the valid votes, so the margin is 10% of 0.8T = 0.08T.
0.08T = 2,000, so T = 25,000.
Note: 20,000 is only the number of valid votes.

questions.text: A reduction of 20% in the price of sugar enables a person to buy 5 kg more sugar for ₹600. What is the reduced price per kg?
questions.explanation:
The money saved = 20% of ₹600 = ₹120.
This ₹120 buys the extra 5 kg at the reduced price.
Reduced price = 120/5 = ₹24 per kg.
Check: the original price is ₹30, and 600/30 = 20 kg while 600/24 = 25 kg.

questions.text: The price of an article is increased by 10%, then increased again by 20%, and finally decreased by 25%. What is the net percentage change in its price?
questions.explanation:
Use multipliers: 1.10 × 1.20 × 0.75.
1.10 × 1.20 = 1.32, and 1.32 × 0.75 = 0.99.
The final price is 99% of the original, which is a 1% decrease.

questions.text: The length of a rectangle is increased by 20% and its breadth is decreased by 10%. What is the percentage change in its area?
questions.explanation:
Area = length × breadth, so use successive change: a + b + ab/100.
= 20 − 10 + (20 × −10)/100 = 10 − 2 = 8.
The area increases by 8%.

questions.text: A man spends 75% of his income. His income increases by 20% and his expenditure increases by 10%. By what percentage do his savings increase?
questions.explanation:
Let income = 100. Expenditure = 75 and savings = 25.
New income = 120 and new expenditure = 82.5, so new savings = 37.5.
Increase = 12.5 on 25.
Percentage increase = 12.5/25 × 100 = 50%.

questions.text: A man spends 20% of his income on rent, 25% of the remaining on food and 30% of what is left after that on education. He saves the rest, which is ₹12,600. What is his income?
questions.explanation:
The fraction left after each step: 0.80 × 0.75 × 0.70 = 0.42.
So 42% of income = ₹12,600.
Income = 12,600/0.42 = ₹30,000.
Check: 30,000 → 24,000 after rent → 18,000 after food → 12,600 after education.

questions.text: The rate of interest on a savings scheme falls from 8% to 6% per annum. What is the percentage decrease in the rate of interest?
questions.explanation:
The fall is 2 percentage points, but the question asks for the percentage decrease.
Percentage decrease = (8 − 6)/8 × 100 = 2/8 × 100 = 25%.

questions.text: A candidate who scores 30% of the maximum marks fails by 50 marks. Another candidate who scores 42% gets 10 marks more than the pass marks. What percentage of marks is required to pass?
questions.explanation:
The difference between the two scores: 42% − 30% = 12% of the maximum = 50 + 10 = 60 marks.
Maximum marks = 60 × 100/12 = 500.
Pass marks = 30% of 500 + 50 = 150 + 50 = 200.
Pass percentage = 200/500 × 100 = 40%.

questions.text: The price of sugar increases by 25%. A family adjusts its consumption so that its expenditure on sugar increases by only 10%. If the family consumed 30 kg of sugar per month earlier, how much does it consume now?
questions.explanation:
Expenditure = price × consumption.
New expenditure/old expenditure = 1.10, and new price/old price = 1.25.
New consumption = 30 × 1.10/1.25 = 33/1.25 = 26.4 kg.
Note: 24 kg would be correct only if the expenditure stayed the same.

questions.text: In an examination, 60% of the candidates were boys. 75% of the boys and 60% of the girls passed. If 620 candidates failed, how many candidates appeared in the examination?
questions.explanation:
Failed boys = 25% of 60% = 15% of all candidates.
Failed girls = 40% of 40% = 16% of all candidates.
Total failed = 31% of the candidates = 620.
Total = 620 × 100/31 = 2,000.

questions.text: If the numerator of a fraction is increased by 20% and its denominator is decreased by 10%, the fraction becomes 16/21. What is the original fraction?
questions.explanation:
Let the fraction be x/y. Then 1.2x/(0.9y) = 16/21.
(4/3) × (x/y) = 16/21.
x/y = 16/21 × 3/4 = 48/84 = 4/7.
Check: 4.8/6.3 = 48/63 = 16/21. The original fraction is 4/7.

questions.text: When 15% of the wheat produced is lost in grinding, a country can export 30 lakh tonnes of wheat. When only 10% is lost, it can export 40 lakh tonnes. What is the total wheat production of the country? (Assume domestic consumption is the same in both cases.)
questions.explanation:
Reducing the loss from 15% to 10% saves 5% of production.
This 5% shows up as extra exports: 40 − 30 = 10 lakh tonnes.
5% of production = 10 lakh tonnes.
Production = 10 × 100/5 = 200 lakh tonnes.
